items.front: How do you combine a:b and b:c into a:b:c?
items.back: Scale each so the shared term b matches (use LCM of the b-terms), then read a:b:c. e.g. 2:3 & 4:5 → 8:12:15.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Types of Ratios

items.front: Compound ratio of a:b, c:d, e:f?
items.back: (a×c×e) : (b×d×f) — product of antecedents : product of consequents, then simplify.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Types of Ratios

items.back: Third to a,b = b²/a; fourth to a,b,c = bc/a; mean proportional of a,b = √(ab). Proportion: ad = bc.
Direct: x/y constant (more→more). Inverse: xy constant (more→less), e.g. men×days = constant.

items.front: Componendo & dividendo, and its typical use?
items.back: If a/b = c/d then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d). Turns (sum):(difference) into the base ratio, e.g. (m+n):(m−n)=7:3 ⇒ m:n=5:2.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Componendo and Dividendo

items.back: In the ratio of capital×time for each partner; share = (their term/total)×profit. Equal periods ⇒ ratio of capitals only.
items.examPoint: Partnership — profit sharing by capital × time

items.back: (n₁x̄₁ + n₂x̄₂)/(n₁+n₂). Never just average the two means when the group sizes differ.

items.front: Average of consecutive/equally-spaced numbers; first n naturals?
items.back: = middle term = (first+last)/2. Average of first n naturals = (n+1)/2.
items.examPoint: Average of first n natural numbers

items.front: Average change on inclusion / replacement of a member?
items.back: New value = new_avg×(n+1) − old_avg×n. Replacement: new = old + (Δavg × count). e.g. 16th innings raises avg by 3.
items.examPoint: Average change on inclusion / exclusion / replacement of a member

items.back: qty(cheap):qty(dear) = (dear−mean):(mean−cheap). The mean always lies between the two component values.

items.front: Successive replacement of liquid — milk left after n draws?
items.back: milk left = initial × (1 − r/T)ⁿ (r drawn each time, T total). e.g. 20 L, draw 4 twice ⇒ 20×0.8²=12.8 L.
items.examPoint: Successive replacement of liquid in a mixture — (1 − r/T)ⁿ
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Replacement N Times

items.front: Ratio a:b as a percentage of the whole; overlapping-group average?
items.back: a as % of whole = a/(a+b)×100 (not a/b). Overlap term = (Σgroup1 + Σgroup2) − Σall.
